decisions.why: The psalm opens on a string of titles of God, each a word the psalter uses again (fortitúdo, firmaméntum, refúgium, liberátor; then adjútor, protéctor, cornu salútis, suscéptor). fortitúdo → força is the glossary's working word (117:14 Fortitúdo mea, et laus mea Dóminus; also 30:4, 42:2 with the same "fortitúdo mea").

options.label: minha força
options.note: Ruling: the glossary row (open) — plain, and left free by virtus → poder. The possessive without article in the vocative, as Portuguese says it (Senhor, minha força).

options.label: minha fortaleza
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 (que és a minha fortaleza) and DM1962 (minha fôrça … minha fortaleza, for another Hebrew word). Refused as the glossary refuses it: in Brazil a fortaleza is first a fortress — and a fortress would be heard beside refúgio as one more building.

decisions.why: firmaméntum (στερέωμα) is "a support, a prop" (Lewis & Short) and also the vault of heaven — the same Latin word is the sky in 18:2 and 150:1 and God as support here, 24:14 and 70:3 (grep, nine lines). Portuguese firmamento is only the sky. The Latin ear hears both; the Portuguese ear will hear only the sky. Draft 2: the blind reader heard "meu firmamento" FIRST as "my sky" — the fault draft 1 named as the test. Option 1 (esteio) becomes the ruling.

options.label: o meu esteio
options.note: Ruling from draft 2: a concrete prop — a post that holds a thing up — and a living figure in Brazil (o esteio da família); keeps the image of support, which is the sense here. Loses the root firm- and the psalter's link with the sky (18:2, 150:1 will say firmamento). Proposed for 24:14 and 70:3, where God is again the firmaméntum.

options.label: o meu firmamento
options.note: Draft 1: the Latin's word; the blind reader heard it first as "my sky" (critic/v1.ambiguity.json) — a wrong first hearing, which in choir is a fault.

options.label: o meu firme apoio
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: the sense spelled out in two words; keeps firm-.

options.label: a minha firmeza
options.note: Keeps the root in one word; but a quality where the Latin names a thing that holds.

decisions.why: adjútor → auxílio is the glossary's working rendering (117:6–7, 118:114, 9:10, 9:35b); the Latinist has asked for the agent noun auxiliador in each of those psalms. Here the question is sharper: 17:2–3 set four agent nouns side by side (liberátor, adjútor, protéctor, suscéptor) and the Portuguese makes two of them agents (libertador, protetor) and two abstract (auxílio, amparo — D19 settled the latter). HELD AGAINST THE LATINIST: minor on draft 1, MAJOR on draft 2 with the words unchanged — the pattern D24 recorded at 118:114 (minor, then major, then major on the same words) and D27 at 9:10. Weighed, not obeyed: auxílio is the glossary's word in four psalms; auxiliador is long and hardly said; and the same metonymy for suscéptor is settled (D19). If Gustavo wants the agent nouns, option 1 here and option 1 of decision susceptor turn both at once.

options.label: o meu auxílio
options.note: Ruling: the glossary, as held in Pss 9, 117 and 118 (D24). The metonymy is the same as suscéptor → amparo three words later, which is settled.

options.label: o meu auxiliador
options.note: The agent noun the Latinist keeps asking for; it would make the series libertador · auxiliador · protetor regular. Long (five syllables) and hardly said.

decisions.latin: Protéctor meus, et cornu salútis meæ, et suscéptor meus
decisions.why: The Latin carries the titles on without a verb from 17:2 into 17:3c. 17:3b needs a copula (the Deus meus is not a vocative: "et sperábo in eum" follows in the third person); 17:3c can continue the list bare.

options.label: O meu
options.note: Ruling: the list continues without a verb, as the Latin; the verse is heard as more names, after "O meu Deus é o meu auxílio".

options.label: É o meu
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 (É o meu protector): a copula supplied; clearer, heavier at the head of the verse.

decisions.why: protéctor (ὑπερασπιστής, the one who holds a shield over) is in the psalter 19 times (grep); the glossary names protéctor → protetor only as what suscéptor → amparo must stay apart from. This psalm has it three times (17:3c, 17:19, 17:31), beside suscéptor and adjútor in one verse (17:3b–3c). Proposed as a row. Stage two: 17:31 protéctor est ómnium sperántium in se, slot p31, filled from the same option.

options.label: protetor
options.note: Ruling: the cognate, plain; the Latin's agent noun; stays apart from amparo and auxílio. MS1932 protector in all three.

options.label: defensor
options.note: Keeps a shield-bearer's sense (defending); MS1932 uses defensor for suscéptor — the two would cross.

options.label: escudo
options.note: The Hebrew's image (magen), DM1962. Refused: the Latin has an agent noun, not a shield.

decisions.why: suscéptor → amparo is settled (D19): the noun is ἀντιλήμπτωρ, "the one who takes hold of, supports", and amparo keeps one family with suscípere → amparar (17:36a déxtera tua suscépit me will say "me amparou"). HELD AGAINST THE LATINIST: minor on draft 1 ("o meu amparador"), MAJOR on draft 2 with the words unchanged ("aquele que me ampara") — two different fixes on two readings. Weighed under D24: the agent noun amparador is not current Portuguese; the relative clause is three words for one and breaks the list of titles (o meu esteio, o meu refúgio, o meu libertador … o meu amparo). Stage two: 17:36a déxtera tua suscépit me — the verb of the same family (D19: suscéptor → amparo, suscípere → amparar; the pair is heard across the psalm, 17:3c … 17:36a), slot susc36. MS1932's option has his verb there, "me susteve".

options.label: o meu amparo
options.note: Ruling: the settled word (D19), as in 3:4, 53:6, 118:114.

options.label: aquele que me ampara
options.note: The Latinist's fix on draft 2 (major): the agent kept as a clause.

options.label: o meu amparador
options.note: The Latinist's fix on draft 1 (minor): an agent noun Portuguese hardly has.

options.label: o meu defensor
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: an agent noun, but defending is not taking up.

decisions.why: The glossary's open row cornu → chifre names 17:3c among the places it must serve. The image is the Latin's (κέρας σωτηρίας), and the Benedictus has the same phrase (not quoted here from memory).

options.label: o chifre
options.note: Ruling: the concrete image (rule 5), as the glossary row; corno is an insult in Brazil. Douay-Rheims "the horn of my salvation". Risk: the blind reader listed "chifre do altar" as unknown in Ps 117.

options.label: a força
options.note: Explains the image (MS1932 "a minha poderosa salvação" does the same). Refused under D2: an image stays an image.

decisions.why: The participle stands first in the Latin, absolute (no object: the praise is God's, left unsaid).

options.label: Louvando, invocarei o Senhor
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's order, the participle bare, as the Latin; laudáre → louvar (glossary, kept apart from confitéri → dar graças).

options.label: Invocarei o Senhor, louvando-o
options.note: Matos Soares 1932's order; supplies an object the Latin does not have.

decisions.why: inférnus → inferno is an open row held for Gustavo (D22): heard first as the hell of the damned. Here the parallel with death (dolóres mortis, 17:5; láquei mortis, 17:6) makes the sense the realm of the dead; but "dolóres inférni" is the Latin's phrase, and it is still the Latin's word.

options.label: inferno
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's word, as 6:6 and 9:18 have it; DRB "the sorrows of hell"; MS1932 "Dores de inferno".

options.label: dos infernos
options.note: The old plural for the abode of the dead (the glossary's option; the Creed's wording is from memory, unverified). Would read "As dores dos infernos".

options.label: abismo dos mortos
options.note: A paraphrase for the realm of the dead; refused under D2.

decisions.why: Two Latin verbs, one Greek verb (προέφθασάν με in both verses: "came upon me first"). Lewis & Short præoccupo "to seize upon beforehand … to take, catch, detect"; prævenio "to come before, anticipate". By D15's test the Latin's variation is an elegance and one Portuguese verb may serve; the pair also ties the two ends of the rescue together (the snares of death came upon me — they came upon me in the day of my affliction). Draft 2: in 17:6 the subject comes first (the stylist: the enclisis after a long verb, then the subject, made the colon laborious) — order only; the Latinist's minor on 17:19 (prævenire is to come first, not to surprise) is refused, see audit.

options.label: surpreender, both
options.note: Ruling: Matos Soares 1932's verb in 17:6, carried to 17:19 (the Greek's one verb). The hostile "coming upon first" is heard; nothing added.

options.label: kept apart: surpreender / anteciparam-se a
options.note: Keeps the Latin's two verbs apart; anteciparam-se a mim is stiff and is left to anticipáre (76:5).

options.label: apanhar / atacar
options.note: MS1932 at 17:19 (atacaram-me) — it interprets the coming-first as an attack.

decisions.latin: in conspéctu ejus / meo / oculórum ejus
decisions.why: in conspéctu four times in the first half: the glossary proposes à vista de (Ps 5, 9) and notes that it fails with verbs of motion, where Ps 118 used a vossa presença. Here two builds: the phrase qualifies a noun (clamor meus in conspéctu ejus, 7b; fulgóre in conspéctu ejus, 13) or is a predicate with a place (judícia ejus in conspéctu meo, 23; in conspéctu oculórum ejus, 25).

options.label: presença with a noun, vista as predicate
options.note: Ruling: à vista de where it is a predicate (the glossary proposal, and "à vista dos seus olhos" keeps oculórum), a noun phrase where it hangs on a noun and a verb of motion follows (7b entrou), as 118:168–170 did. The noun of seeing kept in the two places where it reads, presence in the other two. Draft 3: in 17:13 it stands between commas ("Diante do clarão, na sua presença, passaram as nuvens"), after the genitive of draft 2 was refused by the Latinist.

options.label: à vista everywhere
options.note: One rendering for the phrase; 7b "o meu clamor, à sua vista, entrou" and 13 "Ao fulgor à sua vista" are stiff.

options.label: diante de everywhere
options.note: Douay-Rheims "before him … in my sight … before his eyes"; MS1932 "diante de mim". Plain; loses the noun.

decisions.latin: Commóta est … conturbáta sunt, et commóta sunt
decisions.why: Three passive perfects of motion (ἐσαλεύθη … ἐταράχθησαν καὶ ἐσαλεύθησαν). The Latin repeats commovéri, and the Portuguese repeats one verb for it. The voice: a passive with middle sense, as elsewhere in the glossary rendered by the pronominal form (8:2b se elevou; 7:7a exaltai-vos). The earth is not said to be shaken BY anyone; it shook.

options.label: pronominal: se abalou … se perturbaram e se abalaram
options.note: Ruling: the middle sense, which is what the Portuguese pronominal says; one verb twice for commovéri; conturbáre → perturbar (glossary, tried on bones, soul, eye in Ps 6). MS1932 "abalaram-se".

options.label: passive: foi abalada … foram perturbados e foram abalados
options.note: The voice to the letter; heavier (foram … foram), and it suggests an agent.

options.label: estremeceram (for conturbáta)
options.note: MS1932 "estremeceram" for the foundations; but estremecer is taken by contrémuit in the first colon.

decisions.why: The plain word for smoke.

options.label: fumaça
options.note: Ruling: the Brazilian word (DM1962 "Uma fumaça").

options.label: fumo
options.note: MS1932; in Brazil fumo is first tobacco.

decisions.why: Three times: coals kindled from the fire (9), and the refrain-like "grando et carbónes ignis" (13, 14 — the Latin repeats it word for word, so the Portuguese does).

options.label: carvões
options.note: Ruling: MS1932 in all three ("carvões de fogo"); carvões that are kindled (9) and then carvões OF fire (13, 14) keep the Latin's sequence — the coal set alight.

options.label: brasas
options.note: DM1962 "brasas de fogo"; plainer, but "brasas foram acesas" says the fire twice.

decisions.why: calígo (γνόφος): "thick air, mist, fog; darkness" (L&S). ténebræ → trevas comes two verses later, so calígo needs its own word. Draft 2: "havia" supplied (the stylist) — an existential verb Portuguese needs after a run of action verbs (D2: supplying a verb is grammar); the blind reader had heard the verbless colon rightly, so this is for the ear only.

options.label: uma névoa escura
options.note: Ruling: the mist and the dark in two plain words; MS1932 "uma nuvem obscura" (nuvem is núbes's, 17:12–13).

options.label: uma névoa escura (no verb)
options.note: Draft 1: verbless, as the Latin. The stylist heard the colon as suspended "as if a word were missing" after the action verbs.

options.label: a escuridão
options.note: One plain word; close to trevas (17:12), which the Latin keeps apart.

options.label: a caligem
options.note: The cognate; literary, needs a footnote.

decisions.why: pónere with a double accusative, "made the darkness his hiding-place". latíbulum: "a hiding-place, lurking-place" (L&S), ἀποκρυφή. The psalm has the same build twice more (17:33 pósuit immaculátam viam meam; 17:35 posuísti ut arcum ǽreum brácchia mea), so the verb chosen here should serve all three. Stage two: the same build twice more, 17:33 pósuit immaculátam viam meam (slot p33) and 17:35 posuísti, ut arcum ǽreum, brácchia mea (slot p35) — pónere + a predicate, three times in the psalm, one verb three times: "fez … fez … fizestes" (option 1 has "pôs … pôs … pusestes"). Draft 5: pónere is said with the verb each build takes in Portuguese — "fazer de" (17:12), "tornar" + adjective (17:33, the stylist's: "fez imaculado" was heard as a calque), "fazer … como" (17:35). The Latin's one verb is neither of them; draft 4's one-verb version is the last option.

options.label: fez das trevas o seu esconderijo

forms.posuit: fez das trevas o seu esconderijo
forms.p35: fizestes os meus braços como um arco de bronze

options.note: Ruling: the Portuguese idiom for pónere + two accusatives (MS1932 "Fez das trevas o lugar do seu retiro"); esconderijo is the plain word for latíbulum.

options.label: pôs as trevas por seu esconderijo

forms.posuit: pôs as trevas por seu esconderijo
forms.p35: pusestes os meus braços como um arco de bronze

options.note: The Latin's verb; the predicative "por" is bookish.

options.label: fez das trevas o seu abrigo

forms.posuit: fez das trevas o seu abrigo
forms.p35: fizestes os meus braços como um arco de bronze

options.note: abrigo loses the hiding (and is near refúgio).

options.label: fez … fez imaculado … fizestes

forms.posuit: fez das trevas o seu esconderijo
forms.p35: fizestes os meus braços como um arco de bronze

options.note: Draft 4: one verb, fazer, all three times; the stylist heard "fez imaculado o meu caminho" as a calque (Portuguese says "tornar" + adjective).

decisions.why: dare vocem is an idiom: to utter, to sound (the Greek ἔδωκεν φωνήν is the same). Portuguese "deu a sua voz" is not said. The phrase returns in 45:7 (dedit vocem suam, mota est terra) and 67:34b (dabit voci suæ vocem virtútis).

options.label: fez ouvir a sua voz
options.note: Ruling: the idiom (MS1932, DM1962); the light verb yields as it does elsewhere in the glossary (laudem dícere → dar louvor). Proposed as a formula for 45:7.

options.label: deu a sua voz
options.note: The Latin's verb; a calque, not said in Portuguese.

options.label: soltou a sua voz
options.note: Idiomatic (soltar a voz) and short; changes the verb as much as option 0.

decisions.why: dissipáre → dissipar is an open row that lists 17:15; ἐσκόρπισεν "scattered". Here the object is people (eos, the enemies). Draft 2: the stylist heard "dissipar" people as translated and the blind reader listed "dissipou" as unknown → "dispersou", the Greek's sense (ἐσκόρπισεν). Cost: it meets dispérgere (88:11 dispersísti inimícos tuos, one Greek root διασκορπίζω with this verse's σκορπίζω); they never stand in one verse. The row dissipáre may keep "dissipar" where the object is a thing (118:126 dissiparam a vossa lei).

options.label: dispersou
options.note: The plainest word; but it is wanted for dispérgere (58:12 Dispérge illos).

options.label: dissipou
options.note: Ruling: the row (one verb for nine verses); "dissipar a multidão" is current Portuguese for scattering people.

options.label: desbaratou
options.note: MS1932: routed; a military sense the Latin does not name.

decisions.why: orbis terræ → o orbe da terra is an open row (Ps 9:8b); the blind reader did not know orbe. Here the plural terrárum. Draft 2: the stylist ("livresca … exige decifração") and the blind reader (orbe unknown — as in Ps 9) → "do mundo". The Latin psalter never uses mundus for the world (grep: mundus is only "clean" — 18:13, 23:4, 50:4, 50:9, 50:12), so "mundo" collides with nothing. Proposed for the whole row (12 lines).

options.label: do mundo
options.note: Douay-Rheims "the foundations of the world"; plain; loses the orb.

options.label: do orbe da terra
options.note: Ruling: the row, so that the phrase is one phrase through the psalter (the plural terrárum is not heard, as in DRB "the world").

options.label: da terra
options.note: MS1932 "os fundamentos da terra"; drops orbis.

decisions.why: The noun of increpáre → repreender (working; shared since D21 with árguere). ἀπὸ ἐπιτιμήσεως: the rebuke at which the sea-bed is laid bare. The same phrase opens 75:7 and 103:7 (Ab increpatióne tua fúgient) and closes 79:17. "ab" is the cause (at, because of), as Douay-Rheims "At thy rebuke".

options.label: À vossa repreensão
options.note: Ruling: the glossary's family; "À" gives the cause as DRB's "At" does and echoes 17:13 "Ao fulgor".

options.label: Pela vossa repreensão
options.note: The cause spelled out; heavier, and "pela … pelo" in the second colon.

options.label: Às vossas ameaças
options.note: MS1932 "às tuas ameaças"; a threat is not a rebuke.

decisions.why: Two verbs of taking (ἔλαβεν … προσελάβετο, "took … took to himself"). accípere → tomar; assúmere wants a second verb with the sense of taking up to oneself.

options.label: recolheu
options.note: Ruling: "took up, took in" — a second verb of taking that says the taking-to-oneself; plain.

options.label: tomou consigo
options.note: The Greek's προσ- spelled out; repeats tomar.

options.label: tirou
options.note: MS1932 "tirou-me da inundação": the direction only, not the taking-to-himself.

decisions.why: ἐστερεώθησαν ὑπὲρ ἐμέ: "they were made strong beyond me" — stronger than I. confortári → fortalecer-se is the open row from 9:20. Draft 2: the stylist heard "acima de mim" as a position in space; the comparison is the Latin's sense (ὑπέρ, "beyond"), so it is said as a comparison, with the Latin's verb (confortári → fortalecer-se) kept against the stylist's "se tornaram mais fortes".

options.label: mais do que eu

forms.super: se fortaleceram mais do que eu

options.note: Ruling from draft 2: the verb kept, the comparison made audible (DRB "too strong for me", MS1932 "mais poderosos do que eu").

options.label: acima de mim
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's preposition (super = above, beyond); open between "more than I" and "over me" as the Latin is.

options.label: contra mim
options.note: A hostile "over me"; one of the two readings only.

options.label: se tornaram mais fortes do que eu

forms.super: se tornaram mais fortes do que eu

options.note: The stylist's line — fíeri for confortári; the verb refused, the comparison taken.

decisions.why: edúcere: "lead out, bring out"; latitúdo → amplidão is the glossary row, which names this verse.

options.label: fez sair
options.note: Ruling: keeps the e- (out) and the leading; "E me fez sair para a amplidão".

options.label: levou
options.note: "E me levou para a amplidão": plainer; the out is lost.

options.label: tirou
options.note: MS1932 "Retirou-me"; "tirar para" is not idiomatic.

decisions.why: velle → querer (glossary). "vóluit me" with a person as object: he wanted me, he took pleasure in me (ἠθέλησέν με).

options.label: me quis
options.note: Ruling: the glossary verb; "porque me quis" is heard in Brazil as "because he wanted me / loved me", which is the Latin's range.

options.label: se agradou de mim
options.note: Douay-Rheims "because he was well pleased with me": the sense, another verb.

options.label: me amava
options.note: MS1932 "porque me amava": dilígere's verb (17:2 Díligam → amarei).

decisions.latin: retríbuet mihi … retríbuet mihi (17:21) · retríbuet mihi (17:25)
decisions.why: The Latin says retríbuet three times, and 17:25 repeats the first colon of 17:21 word for word: the stanza on the psalmist's innocence is framed by it. Matos Soares 1932 varies (retribuirá … recompensará).

options.label: me retribuirá, three times
options.note: Ruling: one verb three times (rule 2; glossary retribúere → retribuir outside the vós imperative); 17:21a = 17:25a word for word.

options.label: retribuirá … recompensará
options.note: Matos Soares 1932's variation; refused — it drops a repetition the Latin has.

decisions.latin: nec ímpie gessi a Deo meo
decisions.why: "ímpie gérere a Deo" calques ἠσέβησα ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ μου: to act impiously away from God, i.e. to depart from him in impiety. The preposition is one of separation; Douay-Rheims and Matos Soares both render it "against". The Latinist (draft 1, MAJOR): "contra" loses the separation. Taken.

options.label: me apartei impiamente do meu Deus

forms.impie: me apartei impiamente do meu Deus

options.note: Ruling from draft 2, on the Latinist's major: the calque ἠσέβησα ἀπό says departing from God in impiety, and "a Deo" is separation; the light verb gessi yields to that sense, as his fix does. "apartei", not his "afastei", so that 17:23 non répuli a me → "não afastei de mim" keeps its own verb (two Latin verbs, two Portuguese).

options.label: me afastei impiamente do meu Deus

forms.impie: me afastei impiamente do meu Deus

options.note: The Latinist's exact fix; one verb with 17:23 afastei, which is répuli's.

options.label: agi como ímpio contra o meu Deus

forms.impie: agi como ímpio contra o meu Deus

options.note: Draft 1: both Vulgate-family versions ("against"); the Latinist marked the lost separation major.

options.label: agi como ímpio, longe do meu Deus

forms.impie: agi como ímpio, longe do meu Deus

options.note: Keeps both the acting and the separation; heard as "while far from God".

decisions.why: The Latin's plural justítiæ stands for δικαιώματα here (the Greek word that is justificatiónes → preceitos in Ps 118). The glossary row justítiæ (plural) asks that these places decide locally, "preceitos may be wanted". But the Latin chose justítia, and this stanza is built on it: justítiam meam (21) — justítias ejus (23) — justítiam meam (25).

options.label: as suas justiças
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's word, keeping the stanza's echo (my justice / his justices); 10:8 has "as justiças" and it was never heard as the courts. Douay-Rheims "his justices".

options.label: os seus preceitos
options.note: The Greek's sense (δικαιώματα) and MS1932's word; loses the echo and renders the Greek, not the Latin.

decisions.why: cum eo (μετ᾿ αὐτοῦ): "with him". The next stanza is built on cum (17:26–27 Cum sancto sanctus eris), so the preposition should stay.

options.label: com ele
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's preposition, which 17:26–27 will repeat four times.

options.label: diante dele
options.note: MS1932 "sem mácula diante dele": in conspéctu's phrase.

decisions.why: observáre is a second verb of keeping two verses after custodívi (17:22); the Greek has one verb in both (ἐφύλαξα … φυλάξομαι). Reflexive with ab: to keep oneself from.

options.label: me guardarei
options.note: Ruling: the Greek's one verb (D15's test) and the Portuguese idiom "guardar-se de"; MS1932 "guardar-me-ei da minha iniquidade".

options.label: me acautelarei
options.note: Keeps the verbs apart; "acautelar-se de" is to beware of — close, bookish.

options.label: me observarei
options.note: The cognate; "observar-se" is to watch oneself, not to keep away from.

decisions.why: The Latin says fundaménta twice in the theophany (the mountains' foundations shake; the world's foundations are laid bare), and the Greek has τὰ θεμέλια twice. The stylist, finding 17:8's second colon too long for one breath, proposed alicerces there.

options.label: fundamentos, twice
options.note: Ruling: one word twice, as the Latin (rule 2). The breath is eased instead by dropping the supplied "ele" (the Latin leaves the subject in the verb).

options.label: alicerces / fundamentos
options.note: The stylist's word in 17:8 (with "pois" for quóniam): shorter by nothing, and it breaks the repetition. Refused.

options.label: alicerces, twice
options.note: The plainer word in both places, keeping the repetition; fundamento is as current as alicerce, so the change buys nothing.

decisions.why: The Latin has no verb: "his tent round about him" is either in apposition to latíbulum (he made darkness his hiding-place, his tent round him — Douay-Rheims) or a nominal sentence of its own. The stylist asked for "estava"; the blind reader could not tell how the tent and the dark water are joined — the Latin's own looseness.

options.label: ao seu redor a sua tenda

forms.v12: ao seu redor a sua tenda

options.note: Ruling: verbless, so that the tent may still be the darkness (apposition) — a verb would decide it is a second thing.

options.label: ao seu redor estava a sua tenda

forms.v12: ao seu redor estava a sua tenda

options.note: The stylist: the ear needs a verb. Refused because "estava" closes the apposition reading.

decisions.why: The stylist's worst line: "Ao fulgor na sua presença passaram as nuvens" — two prepositional phrases before the verb with nothing to hold them. præ is "before, in front of" and, with a noun like this, "because of" (Douay-Rheims "At the brightness"); τηλαύγησις is a far-shining brightness. The blind reader did not know fulgor. Draft 3: the Latinist (v2, MAJOR) refused the genitive "o clarão da sua presença" — it fuses two phrases — and proposed the commas. Taken; a two-comma change proposed by the gate itself, not re-read.

options.label: Diante do clarão, na sua presença,
options.note: Ruling from draft 3, the Latinist's fix on draft 2 (major): in conspéctu ejus is where the clouds pass, not whose the brightness is — so it is set off between commas, not made a genitive. "Diante de" is both "before" and "in the face of" (cause), as præ is; clarão is the plain word for a flash of light (DM1962's word in this verse); the stylist's "Diante do" kept.

options.label: Diante do clarão da sua presença

forms.prae: Diante do clarão da sua presença

options.note: Draft 2 (MS1932's build, "Diante do resplendor da sua presença"): one prepositional phrase before the verb, for the stylist; the Latinist (v2, major) — it fuses two phrases, making the presence the brightness's owner.

options.label: Ao fulgor, na sua presença,
options.note: Draft 1's words (DRB "At the brightness"), with the commas; the stylist's worst line on draft 1, and fulgor was unknown to the blind reader.

options.label: Diante do fulgor, na sua presença,
options.note: The stylist's own line; fulgor was unknown to the blind reader.

decisions.why: The stanza turns on a figure: with the holy you will be holy, with the innocent innocent, with the elect elect — and with the perverse pervertéris, a passive verb where the three before are "eris" + adjective (the Greek has an active verb here, διαστρέψεις, "you will twist"). God is the subject. Douay-Rheims: "thou wilt be perverted". Matos Soares 1932 glosses it away ("serás como ele merece").

options.label: vos pervertereis
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's verb and root, the pronominal form for the passive with middle sense as elsewhere in the glossary; keeps the jolt the Latin keeps — the figure ends on a verb, not on "eris".

options.label: sereis perverso
options.note: The fourth member made like the other three (eris + adjective); the root kept, the verb lost.

options.label: sereis pervertido
options.note: Douay-Rheims to the letter; in Brazil "um pervertido" is first a sexual word.

options.label: sereis como ele merece
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: an explanation. Refused under D2.

decisions.why: transgrédior "step across, pass over"; ὑπερβήσομαι τεῖχος "I shall go over a wall".

options.label: transporei o muro
options.note: Ruling: trans- kept in one plain verb (transpor, to get across or over).

options.label: passarei por cima do muro
options.note: The same, spelled out; three syllables longer.

options.label: trespassarei a muralha
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: trespassar is to pierce through, not to go over.

decisions.why: A hanging nominative: "My God — undefiled is his way" (Douay-Rheims "As for my God, his way is undefiled"). impollútus here, immaculátus in 17:24 and 17:33: the Greek has ἄμωμος in all three, so by D15's test one Portuguese word may serve — and it lets the three be heard as one thread (I shall be blameless with him … his way is blameless … he made my way blameless).

options.label: Imaculado é o caminho do meu Deus

forms.v31: Imaculado é o caminho do meu Deus

options.note: Ruling: the hanging nominative made a genitive (grammar, D2; Matos Soares 1932 "Sem mácula é o caminho do meu Deus"), the adjective first as in the Latin; imaculado for impollútus with 17:24 and 17:33.

options.label: O meu Deus: imaculado é o seu caminho

forms.v31: O meu Deus: imaculado é o seu caminho

options.note: The Latin's build; "O meu Deus" is heard as a vocative and "o seu caminho" then hangs.

options.label: Impoluto é o caminho do meu Deus

forms.v31: Impoluto é o caminho do meu Deus

options.note: The cognate keeps impollútus apart from immaculátus as the Latin does; impoluto is a literary word ("honra impoluta").

decisions.why: D27 rules that 17:31 follows 11:7 (As palavras do Senhor são palavras puras … prata examinada no fogo): outside Ps 118 elóquium is decided locally, and here it is a subject with a genitive, where the clause "o que dissestes" cannot serve. The Latin has no verb (the participle stands in apposition to what goes before).

options.label: as palavras do Senhor examinadas no fogo

forms.eloquia: as palavras do Senhor, examinadas no fogo

options.note: Ruling: D27's wording, verbless as the Latin; examináre → examinar (glossary, 11:7).

options.label: as palavras do Senhor são examinadas no fogo

forms.eloquia: as palavras do Senhor são examinadas no fogo

options.note: A copula supplied (D2); but "são examinadas" is heard as a process going on, where the participle is a state (tried, refined).

options.label: o que o Senhor disse, examinado no fogo

forms.eloquia: o que o Senhor disse, examinado no fogo

options.note: D26's clause, as in Ps 118; D27 ruled it out here.

decisions.latin: præcínxit me virtúte · præcinxísti me virtúte ad bellum
decisions.why: virtus (δύναμις) twice, in one phrase — "girded me with virtus". The glossary's open row gives virtus → poder and keeps it apart from fortitúdo → força, which this psalm has in its first line (17:2 fortitúdo mea).

options.label: poder
options.note: Ruling: the glossary row, so that 17:2 força and 17:33/40 poder stay two words as the Latin's two.

options.label: força
options.note: Douay-Rheims "strength", Matos Soares 1932 "força": the plain word for girding, but it merges virtus with fortitúdo in one psalm.

options.label: vigor
options.note: Physical strength, apart from both; not the glossary's word anywhere else.

decisions.latin: Qui perfécit pedes meos tamquam cervórum
decisions.why: The glossary row perfícere → aperfeiçoar was tried by the Ps 8 agent on this very verse ("17:34 perfécit pedes meos"). καταρτιζόμενος "fitting, making ready".

options.label: aperfeiçoou
options.note: Ruling: the row; "aperfeiçoou os meus pés como os dos cervos".

options.label: fez
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 "que fez os meus pés (velozes) como os dos veados" — his gloss shows the gap the plain verb leaves.

options.label: tornou perfeitos
options.note: The stylist (draft 4): "aperfeiçoou os" is a run of vowels hard to say daily. Refused: the glossary row, and "tornou" would come twice in two verses (17:33).

decisions.why: statúere → firmar is the open row (118:38; 39:3 státuit super petram pedes meos is the same build: to set firm on a height). A present participle after a perfect; ἱστῶν με. Draft 5: the gerund, at the Latinist's request.

options.label: me firmando
options.note: Ruling from draft 5, the Latinist's fix (minor): the Latin's present participle kept as a gerund after the perfect "aperfeiçoou", as the Latin sets perfécit beside státuens; the row's verb (statúere → firmar).

options.label: me firma
options.note: Draft 4: a finite present; the Latinist (minor) — it regularises the Latin's participle.

options.label: me estabelece
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 "me estabeleceu": constitúere's verb (17:44).

options.label: me põe de pé
options.note: The Greek's standing; stare's phrase (17:39).

decisions.why: D27 kept in finem apart from in ætérnum and named this verse as one that decides for itself. The Greek is εἰς τέλος ("to the end, completely"); the verb is corrígere, "set straight" (ἀνώρθωσεν, "set upright"). Here nothing is negated — the failure D27 found at 9:19 was "não … até o fim" — and the verb is a past act, so "para sempre" would make the correcting perpetual.

options.label: até o fim
options.note: Ruling: "to the end", as both Vulgate-family versions have it (Douay-Rheims "unto the end", Matos Soares 1932 "até ao fim"), and as εἰς τέλος says; open between "right up to the end" and "thoroughly" as the Latin is. Not "para sempre": perpetuity is not what a past correcting says. So in finem now has two renderings in the psalter, as D27 foresaw — "para sempre" where it says perpetuity (9:7a, 9:19, 12:1), "até o fim" here.

options.label: para sempre
options.note: The working rendering of the glossary row (D27); with a perfect it says "once for all", which the Latin does not.

options.label: de todo
options.note: The "completely" sense of εἰς τέλος alone; closes the openness.

decisions.why: dilatáre → dilatar is the open row for the heart (118:32); with steps it is the widening of the way beneath the feet (ἐπλάτυνας). The psalm has latitúdo → amplidão in 17:20, of the same image.

options.label: Alargastes
options.note: Ruling: the plain verb for widening a path; "dilatar os passos" is not said.

options.label: Dilatastes
options.note: The glossary's cognate (118:32 dilatastes o meu coração); odd with steps.

decisions.latin: et non sunt infirmáta vestígia mea
decisions.why: vestígium: "a footstep, track" (the sole of the foot, then the print). ἴχνη "tracks". Both Vulgate-family versions have "feet". infirmári → enfraquecer (glossary).

options.label: as minhas pegadas
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's image kept, as gressus → passos keeps its own in the first colon.

options.label: os meus pés
options.note: Douay-Rheims "my feet", Matos Soares 1932 "os meus pés": the sense, but pes has its own word in 17:34 and 17:39.

decisions.why: defícere → desfalecer (open row); the row found at 11:2 that desfalecer fails with a person as subject meaning "is gone". Here the sense is "until they give out" (ἐκλίπωσιν), in battle.

options.label: desfaleçam
options.note: Ruling, to be tested: the row's verb; of an enemy pursued, "until they faint" is the sense, not "until they are gone".

options.label: se acabem
options.note: Until they come to an end — the plain verb; closer to Douay-Rheims "till they are consumed".

options.label: sejam aniquilados
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: a passive and a stronger verb than the Latin's.

decisions.why: confríngere → quebrar (open; the same Greek family as contérere — here ἐκθλίψω, "crush").

options.label: quebrarei
options.note: Ruling: the row.

options.label: despedaçarei
options.note: The row's named option if confríngere must stand apart from frángere.

options.label: esmagarei
options.note: The Greek's crushing; another verb.

decisions.latin: et supplantásti insurgéntes in me subtus me
decisions.why: supplánto: "to trip up one's heels, to throw down" (L&S) — the planta, the sole, is in the word. 16:13 supplánta eum, 36:31, 139:5 supplantáre gressus meos are the other places.

options.label: derrubastes
options.note: Ruling: "throw down", plain; "debaixo de mim" (subtus me) carries the rest.

options.label: fizestes tropeçar
options.note: Keeps the tripping, which fits 36:31 and 139:5 (gressus); three syllables longer in an already long colon.

options.label: abatestes
options.note: Matos Soares 1932.

options.label: suplantastes
options.note: The cognate: in Portuguese it means to surpass. Refused.

decisions.latin: Et inimícos meos dedísti mihi dorsum
decisions.why: A double accusative: "you gave me my enemies (as) back" — made them show me their backs, in flight (τοὺς ἐχθρούς μου ἔδωκάς μοι νῶτον). Draft 5: the stylist's wording.

options.label: E me destes as costas dos meus inimigos

forms.dorsum: E me destes as costas dos meus inimigos

options.note: Ruling from draft 5, the stylist's (his worst line on draft 4): every word of the Latin kept — dedísti, mihi, inimícos, dorsum — with the double accusative turned into a genitive (grammar, D2); "you gave me my enemies' backs" is heard at once as their flight.

options.label: E me destes os meus inimigos de costas

forms.dorsum: E me destes os meus inimigos de costas

options.note: Draft 4: the double accusative kept as "de costas"; the stylist heard "dar alguém de costas" as a body's position, and the blind reader could not tell whether they fled or surrendered.

options.label: E fizestes que os meus inimigos me voltassem as costas

forms.dorsum: E fizestes que os meus inimigos me voltassem as costas

options.note: Douay-Rheims "thou hast made my enemies turn their back upon me": the sense, another verb.

decisions.latin: Clamavérunt, nec erat qui salvos fáceret ad Dóminum
decisions.why: "ad Dóminum" stands at the end of the colon, after the clause it does not belong to: they cried — and there was none to save them — to the Lord (Douay-Rheims keeps the order).

options.label: Clamaram ao Senhor, e não havia quem os salvasse

forms.v42: Clamaram ao Senhor, e não havia quem os salvasse

options.note: Ruling: the phrase joined to its verb (order, D2); nothing added.

options.label: Clamaram, e não havia quem os salvasse, ao Senhor

forms.v42: Clamaram, e não havia quem os salvasse, ao Senhor

options.note: The Latin's order; "salvasse ao Senhor" is heard as "save the Lord".

options.label: Clamaram, e não havia quem os salvasse; clamaram ao Senhor

forms.v42: Clamaram, e não havia quem os salvasse; clamaram ao Senhor

options.note: Matos Soares 1932 supplies "(clamaram)" in brackets. Refused: adds a verb.

decisions.why: commínuo: "to break or crumble to pieces" (L&S); λεπτυνῶ "grind fine". deléo: "blot out, efface"; the verb of 50:3b (dele iniquitátem meam).

options.label: esmigalharei … apagarei
options.note: Ruling: crumbling to pieces, as the dust the simile names; delére → apagar, the verb Ps 50:3b will want.

options.label: reduzirei a pó … apagarei
options.note: The image anticipated: "a pó … como o pó" says the dust twice.

options.label: desfarei … esmagarei
options.note: Matos Soares 1932's verbs; esmagar is not delére.

decisions.why: contradíctio (ἀντιλογία): gainsaying, opposition in words; 30:21 a contradictióne linguárum, 80:8 and 105:32 aquam contradictiónis. Draft 5: the blind reader heard "as contradições do povo" FIRST as the people's inconsistencies or internal disagreements, "not evidently directed against the speaker" — the fault draft 4 feared. → "contendas" (strife, disputes), which the psalter does not need for another word (no contentio in the psalms, grep).

options.label: contendas
options.note: Ruling from draft 5: the sense of ἀντιλογία (gainsaying, strife) in a plain word; the cognate is kept as the option, and for 80:8 / 105:32 aquam contradictiónis, a proper name, it may stay.

options.label: contradições
options.note: Ruling, to be tested: the Latin's word (Douay-Rheims, Matos Soares 1932); "sinal de contradição" keeps the sense of opposition alive in church Portuguese. Risk: heard as logical inconsistency.

decisions.why: "at the hearing of the ear" (εἰς ἀκοὴν ὠτίου): they obeyed as soon as they heard — the ear named, as the Latin names it.

options.label: ao ouvir com o ouvido
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's pleonasm kept (hearing, ear).

options.label: mal me ouviu
options.note: The sense in speech; the ear lost.

options.label: ao ouvir a minha voz
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: a voice supplied, the ear lost.

decisions.why: aliénus → estranho (glossary: wider than estrangeiro, anyone not one's own). The Latin says the phrase twice and so does the Portuguese.

options.label: filhos estranhos
options.note: Ruling: the glossary word; Matos Soares 1932 "Os filhos estranhos". Risk: "estranho" is also "odd".

options.label: filhos alheios
options.note: Other people's sons — exactly "not one's own"; not the glossary's word.

options.label: filhos de estrangeiros
options.note: The plainest sense; narrows aliénus to foreign.

decisions.why: claudico "to limp, be lame"; ἐχώλαναν. With a (ἀπό): they limped away from their paths. Draft 5: "coxearam" was listed as unknown by the blind reader and called uncurrent by the stylist, who asked for "mancaram" → taken.

options.label: mancaram
options.note: Ruling from draft 5: the everyday Brazilian verb for limping; plain rather than colloquial in a verse of image.

options.label: coxearam
options.note: Ruling: the plain verb for limping in written Portuguese.

options.label: claudicaram
options.note: The cognate (Matos Soares 1932); literary.

decisions.why: exaltáre → exaltar (glossary); the jussive passive. Ps 9:33 exaltétur manus tua → "exalte-se a vossa mão".

options.label: exalte-se
options.note: Ruling: as 9:33, the pronominal jussive.

options.label: seja exaltado
options.note: The passive to the letter (Matos Soares 1932 "Seja exaltado").

decisions.why: D5: confitéri (to God) → dar graças a.

options.label: darei graças
options.note: Ruling: D5, the dative kept ("vos darei graças"), as 9:2.

options.label: louvarei
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 "te louvarei"; laudáre's verb (17:4 Laudans → Louvando). Refused by D5.

decisions.why: psalmum dícere renders ψαλῶ, the verb that psállere renders elsewhere (7:18 psallam nómini Dómini → entoarei salmos ao nome). By D15's test the Latin's variation is an elegance, and D25's wording can serve with the Latin's noun in the singular.

options.label: entoarei um salmo
options.note: Ruling: D25's verb with the Latin's singular noun; the colon echoes 7:18b "e entoarei salmos ao nome …".

options.label: direi um salmo
options.note: The Latin's verb; "dizer um salmo" is said, but thin.

options.label: cantarei um salmo
options.note: Matos Soares 1932, Douay-Rheims "sing"; cantar is cantáre's.

decisions.latin: Magníficans salútes Regis ejus, et fáciens misericórdiam
decisions.why: The psalm ends on two participles that hang on nothing in the verse (the Latin turns to the third person: Regis ejus, Christo suo). magnificáre → engrandecer (glossary). salútes is plural (σωτηρίας): kept.

options.label: Engrandecendo as salvações do seu Rei

forms.magnificans: Engrandecendo as salvações do seu Rei

options.note: Ruling: the participles as gerunds, dangling as the Latin's do (the glossary row "participle + finite verb → gerund"); the plural kept.

options.label: Ele engrandece as salvações do seu Rei

forms.magnificans: Ele engrandece as salvações do seu Rei

options.note: A subject and a finite verb supplied (the second participle would follow: "e usa de misericórdia"); clearer, and it decides that the subject is God.

options.label: Engrandecendo a salvação do seu Rei

forms.magnificans: Engrandecendo a salvação do seu Rei

options.note: The plural made singular, as usage prefers; the Latin's number is lost.

decisions.why: semen for offspring, the Latin's (and the Greek's) image. In Portuguese "a sua semente" for descendants belongs to older Bibles; the ear hears seed.

options.label: descendência
options.note: Ruling: the plain word; the image is the language's, not the psalm's own figure.

options.label: semente
options.note: Douay-Rheims "his seed": the image kept.

options.label: posteridade
options.note: Matos Soares 1932.

decisions.why: cervus: the hart. The blind reader heard "os meus pés como os dos cervos" as "the feet of SERVANTS" — cervo and servo sound alike in Brazil, and "servos" is the likelier word in church. The other places (28:9 cervos, 41:2 cervus ad fontes aquárum, 103:17 cervis) have the animal's context around them; here nothing but "pés" follows.

options.label: das corças
options.note: Ruling from draft 5: the same animal, the female; no homophone; the Latin's plural kept. Cost: the gender (cervórum is masculine) — a hind for a hart.

options.label: dos cervos
options.note: Draft 4: the Latin's word; heard by the blind reader as "servos".

options.label: dos veados
options.note: Matos Soares 1932's word, the everyday Brazilian name of the animal; in Brazil "veado" is also a slur, which in choir would be heard.

decisions.latin: et disciplína tua ipsa me docébit
decisions.why: ipsa marks the repeated subject: "and your discipline — it — will teach me". The repetition of disciplína tua is kept either way.

options.label: a vossa própria disciplina
options.note: Ruling from draft 5, the stylist: "ela mesma" between two pauses broke the colon and sounded explanatory; "própria" is how Portuguese says ipsa with a noun.

options.label: a vossa disciplina, ela mesma,
options.note: Draft 4: the pronoun set off, as the Latin's ipsa after the noun.

options.label: essa vossa mesma disciplina
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 ("essa tua mesma disciplina"); heavier.

decisions.latin: subtus me (17:37, 17:40) · subtus pedes meos (17:39) · sub me (17:48)
decisions.why: The Latin says subtus three times in four verses (the steps widened under me, the enemies fall under my feet, those who rose against me thrown down under me), and sub me in 17:48 (the peoples subjected under me). One Portuguese preposition throughout keeps the thread.

options.label: sob
options.note: Ruling from draft 5: the stylist asked for "sob mim" in 17:40 (the colon was heavy and "debaixo de mim" delayed the object) and in 17:48; taken in all four places so that the repetition stays one word. 17:10 sub pédibus ejus already has "sob os seus pés".

options.label: debaixo de
options.note: Draft 4: the plainer preposition in speech, and 8:8's "debaixo dos seus pés"; one syllable or two longer each time.

decisions.latin: Qui docet manus meas ad prǽlium
decisions.why: docére → ensinar (glossary). The psalm says it twice, one verse apart: docet (17:35) and docébit (17:36b, "me ensinará") — the hands taught for battle, the man taught by discipline.

options.label: ensina
options.note: Ruling: the glossary verb, which keeps the echo with 17:36b.

options.label: instrui
options.note: The stylist (draft 4): "ensinar as mãos para" leaves the ear waiting for another construction. Refused: it breaks the echo, and instruir is erudíre's (2:10).

options.label: adestra
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 ("que adestra as minhas mãos para a peleja"): the idiom for training hands, another verb.

choices.17:2: The psalm begins at 17:2 (17:1 is the titulus; D7). The inline marker (3a) is not reproduced. dilígere → amar (glossary); "Eu vos amarei" supplies the subject so that the verse does not open on a clitic. refúgium → refúgio, liberátor → libertador. The copula "é" is supplied in the second colon (D2), as DRB does.
choices.17:3b: speráre in → esperar em (glossary). "Deus meus" is not a vocative: the second colon speaks of him in the third person, so the copula is supplied (DRB, MS1932).
choices.17:3c: suscéptor → amparo (settled, D19). The four agent nouns of 17:2–3 come out as two agents (libertador, protetor) and two abstracts (auxílio, amparo) — see decision adjutor.
choices.17:4: invocáre → invocar; salvus ero → serei salvo.
choices.17:5: circumdáre → cercar; conturbáre → perturbar (glossary). Articles supplied (as dores da morte, as torrentes da iniquidade) so that 17:5 and 17:6 match: dolóres mortis / dolóres inférni / láquei mortis. The Greek ὠδῖνες are birth-pangs; the Latin dolóres is pain, and the Portuguese follows the Latin.
choices.17:6: láqueus → laço (glossary). The subject stands after the verb as in the Latin (præoccupavérunt me láquei mortis).
choices.17:7a: tribulátio → tribulação, clamáre → clamar (glossary). Natural order in the second colon.
choices.17:7b: exaudíre → escutar (D3). "ele" supplied so that "do seu templo santo" is not heard as the voice's origin. templum sanctum → templo santo (5:8b).
choices.17:8: irásci → irar-se (glossary); eis → contra eles (MS1932). "ele" supplied: the Latin leaves the subject in the verb (the Greek adds ὁ θεός).
choices.17:9: a fácie ejus → da sua face (glossary: a fácie → da face de); exardéscere → inflamar-se (117:12). "ab eo" → "por ele", open between God and the fire as the Latin is (DRB "by it").
choices.17:10: The second colon has no verb in the Latin and none is supplied.
choices.17:11: volávit, volávit: the repetition kept. pennæ → asas (open row; collides with alæ, which this psalm does not have). Chérubim lowercase, as ángelus → anjo.
choices.17:12: in circúitu → ao redor (glossary); tabernáculum → tenda (open). "tenebrósa" echoes "ténebras" in the Latin, and "tenebrosa" echoes "trevas" only faintly; kept.
choices.17:13: præ with the ablative is cause (Douay-Rheims "At the brightness"): "Ao fulgor" keeps it without spelling it out. fulgor → fulgor (the family of fúlgura in 17:15, which Portuguese cannot keep: relâmpagos). grando → granizo (Brazilian; saraiva is European). The second colon is verbless, as the Latin.
choices.17:14: The second colon repeats 17:13's word for word, as the Latin does.
choices.17:15: míttere → enviar, here and in 17:17 (Misit de summo), one verb twice. sagítta → seta (glossary). "et dissipávit eos … et conturbávit eos": the parallel endings kept (os dissipou … os perturbou).
choices.17:16a: reveláre → desvendar (the glossary's verb for reveláre, 118:18); the passive kept. The colon ends on ":" as the Latin, which runs on into 17:16b.
choices.17:16b: The address turns to God in mid-description (tua … tuæ); vós. inspirátio (ἐμπνεύσεως) → sopro; spíritus → espírito (kept: the breath of the spirit of your wrath, the Latin's two nouns).
choices.17:17: Misit with no object, as the Latin and DRB ("He sent from on high"); MS1932 supplies "a sua mão". de aquis multis → de muitas águas, no article, as the phrase is usually said.
choices.17:18: erípere de + me → arrancar (glossary: with a source named, arrancar is untouched). odérunt is a perfect with present sense (odi): "que me odeiam". confortári → fortalecer-se (open row, 9:20).
choices.17:19: afflíctio → aflição. fíeri → fazer-se (open row): "se fez o meu protetor".
choices.17:21: púritas → pureza. The Latin's final ":" (the sentence runs into 17:22) becomes a full stop in the draft's punctuation, since 17:22 opens with its own "Porque".
choices.17:23: judícia → juízos (D15); repéllere a → afastar de (glossary). The order of the second colon made natural (e não afastei de mim as suas justiças).
choices.17:25: The first colon is 17:21's, word for word (decision retribuet). Stage one ends here: 17:21 and 17:25 frame the psalmist's account of his innocence, and 17:26 turns to address God (Cum sancto sanctus eris) — see audit.
choices.17:26: The address turns to God ("eris", second person — vós, sereis). sanctus (ὅσιος) → santo; vir → homem; ínnocens → inocente. The figure (with X you will be X) kept four times, the adjective repeated each time.
choices.17:28: húmilis → humilde (D27) and humiliáre → humilhar: the Latin's echo húmilem … humiliábis is heard (humilde … humilhareis). superbus → soberbo. salvum fácere → salvar.
choices.17:29: lucérna → lâmpada (glossary); illumináre → iluminar, twice as the Latin. Rule 3: "iluminai" is safe (past "iluminei").
choices.17:30: in te … in Deo meo → "em vós … no meu Deus", the Latin's preposition twice (Douay-Rheims "by thee … through my God"). erípere a → arrancar (glossary). tentátio → tentação (the Latin's reading; the Hebrew has a troop).
choices.17:31: speráre in → esperar em. "ele é" supplied for "protéctor est" so that the colon does not open on a bare noun.
choices.17:32: præter → senão (Douay-Rheims "but"), twice as the Latin; the double question kept.
choices.17:33: "É Deus que" — the Latin's Deus, qui continues the answer to 17:32 ("who is God but our God? God, who …"); a copula supplied so that the three relatives of 17:33–35 have something to hang on. præcíngere → cingir.
choices.17:34: cervus → cervo; "como os dos cervos" supplies the pronoun (tamquam cervórum, genitive). excélsa → as alturas.
choices.17:35: docére → ensinar (glossary) — and 17:36b docébit → ensinará, the echo kept. prǽlium → batalha, bellum (17:40) → guerra. The Latin turns to the second person in mid-verse (posuísti); so does the Portuguese (fizestes).
choices.17:36a: protéctio → proteção (glossary); salútis tuæ → "da vossa salvação" (the Latin's tuæ, not the Greek's μου). déxtera → a direita (glossary).
choices.17:36b: disciplína → disciplina (glossary), twice; "ela mesma" for ipsa, set off, so that the repetition is heard as the Latin's emphasis.
choices.17:37: gressus → passos; subtus → debaixo de, all three times in the psalm (17:37, 39, 40).
choices.17:38: pérsequi → perseguir, comprehéndere → prender (glossary rows; this verse is in the row's list); convérti → voltar, with "atrás" as Portuguese says "turn back".
choices.17:39: stare → estar de pé (glossary). "Eu" supplied so that the verse does not open on a clitic.
choices.17:40: insúrgere in → levantar-se contra (glossary); the present participle after a perfect → imperfect (os que se levantavam). A long colon (the Latin is 14 syllables); accepted for the two phrases the Latin has.
choices.17:41: dispérdere → exterminar (glossary); odiéntes me → os que me odeiam (17:18 has the same phrase).
choices.17:42: exaudíre → escutar (D3); "ele" supplied: the subject changes from them to the Lord.
choices.17:43: ante fáciem → diante da face de (glossary); plátea → rua (Matos Soares 1932 "das ruas"; a plátea is a broad street).
choices.17:44: erípere de → arrancar (glossary); constitúere → estabelecer (glossary); in caput → como cabeça. gentes → nações (glossary); 17:50 natiónes → nações too (one Greek word, ἔθνη).
choices.17:45: cognóvi: the perfect of knowing, "que eu não conhecia"; servíre → servir; obedíre → obedecer.
choices.17:46: inveteráre → envelhecer (glossary, which names 17:46); sémita → vereda (D15); "fora das suas veredas" for a sémitis suis (the separation of ἀπό).
choices.17:47: Vivit Dóminus: "Vive o Senhor". "bendito o meu Deus" verbless, as the Latin, open between a statement and a wish (117:26a "Bendito o que vem" has the same build).
choices.17:48: vindíctæ → vinganças (plural kept); subdere → sujeitar (the glossary's verb for subjícere, 8:8 — one Greek verb, ὑποτάσσω; 143:2 qui subdit pópulum meum sub me will follow); iracúndus → irado. The second colon is a vocative, like 17:2 "Senhor, minha força".
choices.17:49: exaltáre → exaltar; ab insurgéntibus → "acima dos que se levantam" (Douay-Rheims "above them that rise up"); vir iníquus → homem iníquo; erípere → arrancar.
choices.17:51: Christus → Cristo (D19); David → Davi. misericórdiam fácere cum → usar de misericórdia com (the light verb yields, as bonitátem fácere cum → usar de bondade com, 118:65). usque in sǽculum → para sempre (in sǽculum, glossary).

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm17.txt: 54 prayed verses 17:2–17:51 with DO's split ids (17:3b, 17:3c, 17:7a, 17:7b, 17:16a, 17:16b, 17:36a, 17:36b; there is no 17:3a — the first colon of Vulgate verse 3 is inside 17:2, after the inline marker (3a), which is not reproduced). 17:1 is the titulus (D7). Douay-Rheims checked against the Latin at both ends (Bolls chapter 18): 17:2 'I will love thee, O Lord, my strength' = Díligam te, Dómine, fortitúdo mea; 17:51 'Giving great deliverance to his king, and shewing mercy to David his anointed: and to his seed for ever' = Magníficans salútes Regis ejus … usque in sǽculum. The Diurnal Monástico 1962 in the dossier breaks off at Hebrew v. 25. Worked in two stages in one folder, as Ps 9 was: 17:2–17:25 first, then 17:26–17:51 appended. While partial, prayed.json and literal.json carry 'range'; ps017/partial.py (copied from ps009/partial.py) stands in for checks.py, ps017/part.py (from ps009/part.py) builds the critics' sub-folder for stage two. The parallel text 2 Samuel (2 Kings) 22 is not used: its Vulgate is Jerome's version from the Hebrew, not a witness of the Gallican Latin.

Stage one (17:2–17:25), draft 1, from consult/parallels/ps017.md (LXX Rahlfs, Douay-Rheims, Matos Soares 1932 text layer, DM1962 for diction; DO's Portuguese not used, D12). Why the stage ends at 17:25: it is the 27th of the 54 prayed verses, and it closes the unit 17:21–25, framed by the same colon (Et retríbuet mihi Dóminus secúndum justítiam meam) — the psalmist's account of his innocence; 17:26 opens a new movement addressed to God (Cum sancto sanctus eris … Quóniam tu …). Lewis & Short read for præoccupo, latíbulum, firmaméntum. Repeats found with ps005/grep_latin.py: firmaméntum 9 lines (sky in 18:2 and 150:1, support here, 24:14, 70:3); protéctor 19 lines (three in this psalm); 'Ab increpatióne tua' also 75:7, 103:7; 'fortitúdo mea' 30:4, 42:2, 117:14. Glossary applied: dilígere → amar, fortitúdo → força, refúgium, adjútor → auxílio, suscéptor → amparo (D19), speráre in, laudáre → louvar, invocáre, circumdáre → cercar, conturbáre → perturbar, láqueus → laço, tribulátio, clamáre, exaudíre → escutar (D3), irásci, exardéscere → inflamar-se, a fácie → da face, pennæ → asas, in circúitu, tabernáculum → tenda, sagítta → seta, dissipáre → dissipar, orbis terræ → orbe da terra, increpáre (noun) → repreensão, erípere de → arrancar, confortári → fortalecer-se, latitúdo → amplidão, salvum fácere, velle → querer, retribúere → retribuir, custodíre → guardar, judícia → juízos (D15), repéllere a → afastar, immaculátus → imaculado, inférnus → inferno (held for Gustavo, D22). Places where the Latin follows the Greek and the draft follows the Latin: 17:3c 'O meu protetor' (not the Hebrew's shield), 17:6 inferno as dolóres (not cords), 17:17 muitas águas, 17:18 'acima de mim', 17:20 'porque me quis', 17:23 'as suas justiças'. Every vós imperative checked for rule 3: none in stage one (the address to God in 17:16b is by possessives only).

Stage one, draft 1, through ps017/partial.py (checks.py's own code on 17:2–17:25): hard pass (ids and marks). Mended before the critics: 17:18 flex on the proparoxytone 'fortíssimos' → MS1932's order 'dos meus fortíssimos inimigos'; 17:10 'debaixo dos' → 'sob os' (+5 → +2). Soft flags accepted: 17:8 second colon +4 (three verbs and 'ele' supplied; the Latin's own colon is 26 syllables); 17:7a first colon −3, 17:12 flex −4, 17:16b first colon −3, 17:20 second colon −5, 17:25 second colon −5 (Latin polysyllables: tribulatióne, tabernáculum, increpatióne, quóniam vóluit, oculórum); 17:16a second colon +3 (orbe da terra). Rhymes accepted as the Latin's own: 17:15 dissipou / perturbou (dissipávit eos / conturbávit eos), 17:13 / 17:14 the same final colon (grando et carbónes ignis twice). Every Portuguese colon ends oxytone or paroxytone.

Stage one, draft 1 (17:2–17:25). Four verses: one major, taken (17:22, the separation in a Deo); three minors refused (17:3b auxiliador and 17:3c amparador under the glossary — D19 and D24; 17:19 the verb, under D15's test). Marks confirmed in all 27 verses. Passed without remark: esteio was not yet there — "o meu firmamento", "o chifre da minha salvação", "As dores do inferno", "surpreenderam-me" (17:6), "se perturbaram e se abalaram", "fez ouvir a sua voz", "À vossa repreensão", "me recolheu", "me fez sair para a amplidão", "porque me quis", "as suas justiças", "com ele", "me guardarei".

outcomes.remark: adjútor = the one who helps; "o meu auxílio" is a defensible metonymy, less personal (minor) → "o meu auxiliador"
outcomes.reason: The glossary (open) as held in Pss 9, 117 and 118 against the same request (D24): auxiliador is long and hardly said; the metonymy is the same as the settled suscéptor → amparo.

outcomes.remark: suscéptor = the one who takes up; "o meu amparo" by metonymy (minor) → "o meu amparador"
outcomes.reason: D19 settles suscéptor → amparo; amparador is not current Portuguese.

outcomes.remark: prævenire is to come first, anticipate; "Surpreenderam-me" substitutes surprise (minor) → "Anteciparam-se a mim"
outcomes.reason: The Greek has one verb (προέφθασαν) for 17:6 præoccupavérunt and 17:19 prævenérunt, so by D15's test one Portuguese verb may serve both; "surpreender" is L&S's "take, catch" for præoccupo and says the hostile coming-first; "anteciparam-se a mim" is stiff and is left to anticipáre (76:5). He passed the same verb in 17:6.

outcomes.remark: "contra" loses the separation of a Deo meo: the phrase is not departing impiously from God (MAJOR) → "e não me afastei impiamente do meu Deus"
outcomes.reason: Right: the Latin calques ἠσέβησα ἀπό. Taken with "apartei" for his "afastei", so that répuli a me (17:23, afastei) keeps its own verb.

audit.note: Stage one, draft 1. Eight verses; best 17:20, worst 17:13. "O salmo tem gravidade, imagens fortes e terminações adequadas ao canto … Os tropeços se concentram nas elipses e construções que ainda seguem de perto a sintaxe latina." Taken: 17:6 order, 17:10 havia, 17:13 Diante do, 17:15 dispersou, 17:16a do mundo, 17:18 the comparison. Refused: 17:8 alicerces / pois, 17:12 estava, the rest of 17:15, the verb of 17:18.

outcomes.remark: the enclisis after a long verb, then the subject, makes the second colon laborious → "os laços da morte me surpreenderam"
outcomes.reason: Order only (D2). The stressed vowels of cercaram / surpreenderam differ, so it is not a rhyme.

outcomes.remark: the second colon asks too much breath → "os alicerces dos montes … pois ele se irou contra eles"
outcomes.reason: alicerces breaks the Latin's repetition fundaménta (17:8, 17:16a); "pois" would give quóniam a second word in a psalm that has porque for it seven times. The breath is eased by dropping the supplied "ele" instead.

outcomes.remark: the verbless colon sounds suspended after the action verbs → "e havia uma névoa escura sob os seus pés"
outcomes.reason: A verb supplied is grammar (D2).

outcomes.remark: two possessives and no verb make the listener rebuild the sentence → "ao seu redor estava a sua tenda"
outcomes.reason: The verb would decide an ambiguity the Latin keeps: whether the tent is the darkness (apposition, DRB) or a second thing.

outcomes.remark: WORST LINE: two prepositional phrases before the verb; the sentence is slow to be understood → "Diante do fulgor na sua presença, passaram as nuvens"
outcomes.reason: Taken as "Diante do clarão da sua presença passaram as nuvens": his "Diante do", one prepositional phrase before the verb (in conspéctu as a genitive, MS1932's build), and "clarão" for fulgor, which the blind reader did not know.

outcomes.remark: "dissipar" people sounds translated; -ou endings sing → "e os dispersou … e os deixou perturbados"
outcomes.reason: "dispersou" taken. "os deixou perturbados" refused: it turns the active verb into a state, and the -ou endings are the Latin's own (dissipávit eos / conturbávit eos).

outcomes.remark: "orbe da terra" is bookish → "os fundamentos do mundo"
outcomes.reason: With the blind reader, who did not know orbe (nor did Ps 9's). The psalter never has mundus for the world, so mundo is free.

outcomes.remark: "acima de mim" sounds spatial → "porque se tornaram mais fortes do que eu"
outcomes.reason: The comparison taken ("se fortaleceram mais do que eu"); his verb refused (fíeri for confortári) and kept as an option of the same decision.

audit.note: Stage one, draft 1, Portuguese only. 31 items, 5 unknown words (torrentes, iniquidade ×2, fulgor, dissipou, orbe). One real fault: 17:2 "meu firmamento" heard first as "my sky" — mended (esteio). Two unknown words replaced (fulgor → clarão, orbe → mundo; dissipou → dispersou with the stylist). The rest are the Latin's own openness heard as the Latin is read: who lit the coals (17:9 por ele), whom he was angry with (17:8 eles), how the tent and the water are joined (17:12), whether the hail "passed" with the clouds (17:13), what was sent (17:17).

outcomes.remark: "meu firmamento" likely heard as "my sky"
outcomes.reason: The wrong first hearing draft 1 set out to test → "o meu esteio".

outcomes.remark: "o chifre da minha salvação" heard as a concrete horn, its link with salvation unclear
outcomes.reason: The Latin's image (rule 5); it was not misheard, only not explained — and the psalm does not explain it.

outcomes.remark: "as dores do inferno" heard as the torments of the damned
outcomes.reason: Held for Gustavo under D22 (inférnus → inferno), with the realm-of-the-dead reading noted; the parallel with death in the same verse leads the ear back.

outcomes.remark: "ele se irou contra eles": against the mountains, or the enemies
outcomes.reason: The Latin's eis is as open; the nearest referent (the mountains) is the Latin's too.

outcomes.remark: "por ele": by the fire or by God
outcomes.reason: The Latin's ab eo is open in the same way (DRB "by it").

outcomes.remark: how "a sua tenda" and "água tenebrosa" are joined is unclear
outcomes.reason: The Latin strings three nominal members without verbs; the Portuguese keeps it.

outcomes.remark: the clouds, the hail and the coals all "passed"
outcomes.reason: That is a possible reading of the Latin too (grando et carbónes in apposition to nubes).

outcomes.remark: "os perturbou" could point back to the lightnings; whom "os dispersou" means is not named
outcomes.reason: Latin eos cannot be the neuter fúlgura, Portuguese "os" can; but the reader himself heard the enemies first, and the parallel "os dispersou … os perturbou" carries it.

outcomes.remark: "o sopro do espírito da vossa ira": possibly heard as the Holy Spirit
outcomes.reason: spíritus is the Latin's noun (breath and spirit at once); rule 2 keeps it.

outcomes.remark: "Enviou do alto": what was sent is not heard
outcomes.reason: The Latin names no object (MS1932 supplies "a sua mão"); kept open.

outcomes.remark: "imaculado com ele" heard as "pure by being with God"
outcomes.reason: cum eo is kept for the stanza that follows (17:26–27 Cum sancto … cum viro …); the reading heard is inside the Latin's range.

outcomes.remark: unknown word: fulgor
outcomes.reason: → clarão (DM1962).

outcomes.remark: unknown word: dissipou
outcomes.reason: → dispersou.

outcomes.remark: unknown word: orbe
outcomes.reason: → mundo.

outcomes.remark: unknown words: torrentes, iniquidade (also 17:24)
outcomes.reason: torrentes is the Latin's image; iniquidade is the glossary word (iníquitas), already listed as unknown elsewhere and kept.

audit.note: Stage one, draft 2 (revise_v2.py; draft 1 kept as prayed.v1.json). 17:2 "o Senhor é o meu esteio" (blind reader); 17:6 "os laços da morte me surpreenderam" (stylist, order); 17:8 "porque se irou contra eles" (supplied "ele" dropped for breath; new decision fundamenta); 17:10 "e havia uma névoa escura" (stylist); 17:12 unchanged, new decision v12; 17:13 "Diante do clarão da sua presença passaram as nuvens" (stylist's worst line; new decision prae); 17:15 "e os dispersou"; 17:16a "os fundamentos do mundo"; 17:18 "porque se fortaleceram mais do que eu"; 17:22 "e não me apartei impiamente do meu Deus" (Latinist major).

Stage one, the gate on draft 2. Three verses, all MAJOR. 17:13 taken (the genitive refused; commas). 17:3b auxílio and 17:3c amparo HELD on purpose — both minors on draft 1 with the same words, majors now; the glossary words of four psalms (D19 settled, D24). Everything changed in draft 2 passed: esteio, "os laços da morte me surpreenderam", "se irou contra eles", "havia uma névoa escura", "dispersou", "do mundo", "se fortaleceram mais do que eu", "me apartei impiamente do meu Deus". Marks confirmed in all 27 verses.

outcomes.remark: adjútor names the one who helps; "o meu auxílio" substitutes the help given (MAJOR) → "o meu auxiliador"
outcomes.reason: Held against the gate: minor on draft 1 with the same words; the glossary word of Pss 9, 117, 118 (held there against the same request, D24, D27); auxiliador is long and hardly said.

outcomes.remark: suscéptor names the one who takes up; "o meu amparo" turns it into an abstraction (MAJOR) → "aquele que me ampara"
outcomes.reason: Held against the gate: settled (D19); minor on draft 1 with the same words and another fix (amparador); the clause breaks the list of titles.

outcomes.remark: "o clarão da sua presença" fuses two phrases: in conspéctu ejus does not say whose the brightness is (MAJOR) → "Diante do clarão, na sua presença, passaram as nuvens"
outcomes.reason: Right: draft 2 made a genitive of an adverbial phrase for the stylist's sake; the commas give the stylist the pause he wanted as well.

audit.note: Stage one, draft 3 (revise_v3.py; draft 2 kept as prayed.v2.json): 17:13 "Diante do clarão, na sua presença, passaram as nuvens" (the gate's fix); a decision susceptor made for 17:3c so that the hold against the gate is recorded where the word is. Not re-read by a critic: a two-comma change proposed by the gate itself. Stage one ends here, at 17:25; its gate stands with two majors held on purpose (17:3b auxílio, 17:3c amparo).

Stage one, drafts 2–3, through ps017/partial.py: hard pass. New soft flags accepted: 17:10 second colon +6 ('havia' supplied for the stylist, and 'uma névoa escura' is three words for calígo — plain words over count); 17:22 second colon +3 (the Latinist's 'me apartei impiamente'). 17:8 is no longer flagged (the supplied 'ele' dropped). The rest as on draft 1.

Stage two (17:26–17:51), appended as draft 4 (append_v4.py; draft 3 kept as prayed.v3.json, literal.v3.json). Glossary applied: húmilis → humilde / humiliáre → humilhar (the echo kept), lucérna → lâmpada, illumináre → iluminar, erípere → arrancar, elóquium → palavras (D27: 17:31 follows 11:7), examináre → examinar, protéctor → protetor (slot p31), virtus → poder (kept apart from 17:2 fortitúdo → força), perfícere → aperfeiçoar (the row was tried on 17:34), statúere → firmar, docére → ensinar, protéctio → proteção, suscípere → amparar (slot susc36 in decision susceptor), déxtera → a direita, disciplína → disciplina, infirmári → enfraquecer, pérsequi → perseguir, comprehéndere → prender, convértere → voltar, confríngere → quebrar, stare → estar de pé, insúrgere in → levantar-se contra, dispérdere → exterminar, exaudíre → escutar, ante fáciem → diante da face, constitúere → estabelecer, aliénus → estranho, inveteráre → envelhecer, sémita → vereda, exaltáre → exaltar (9:33's jussive), confitéri → dar graças (D5), psállere → entoar salmos (D25, for psalmum dícere = ψαλῶ), magnificáre → engrandecer, Christus → Cristo (D19), in sǽculum → para sempre. in finem (17:36b) decided here as D27 asked: 'até o fim', not merged — see decision finem. pónere + predicate three times (17:12, 33, 35) → one verb, fazer (slots p33, p35 in decision posuit). Places where the Latin follows the Greek against the Hebrew and is followed: 17:26–27 (the Latin's 'santo … inocente … eleito … vos pervertereis', not the Hebrew's), 17:30 tentação (not a troop), 17:36a 'da vossa salvação' (the Latin's tuæ against the Greek's μου), 17:36b the disciplina (not the Hebrew's gentleness), 17:37 pegadas, 17:43 lama das ruas, 17:45–46 the Latin's tenses, 17:46 'coxearam fora das suas veredas'. Rule 3: the only vós imperative of stage two is 17:29 'iluminai' (safe).

Draft 4, whole psalm, the ordinary checks.py: exit 0 (hard pass: 54 ids, marks). Mended before the critics: 17:46 'mentiram-me' (proparoxytone at the mediant) → 'me mentiram'. Soft flags accepted in stage two: 17:40 second colon +6 (the two phrases subtus me and insurgéntes in me), 17:44 second colon +5 ('e' supplied, 'como cabeça'), 17:31 last colon +4 ('ele é' supplied), 17:49 +4, 17:35, 17:36b, 17:38, 17:39, 17:43, 17:48 +3; 17:28 −3, 17:50 −4 (Latin polysyllables). Rhymes: none new.

Stage two, draft 4, the new verses only (part2/, 17:26–17:51). One verse, minor: 17:34 the participle státuens made finite — taken. Everything else passes, including the readings the draft thought hardest: "vos pervertereis" (17:27), "Imaculado é o caminho do meu Deus" (17:31), "as palavras do Senhor, examinadas no fogo" (D27), "É Deus que me cingiu de poder", "me corrigiu até o fim" (17:36b, in finem decided here), "E me destes os meus inimigos de costas", the order of 17:42, "entoarei um salmo" for psalmum dicam, the gerunds of 17:51. Marks confirmed.

outcomes.remark: státuens (present participle) turned into a finite indicative, regularising the Latin's perfécit … státuens (minor) → "e sobre as alturas me firmando"
outcomes.reason: Voice, tense and mood are kept where Portuguese can keep them; a gerund can.

audit.note: Stage two, draft 4. Eight verses; best 17:29, worst 17:41. "O salmo tem gravidade e imagens fortes … Os tropeços vêm sobretudo de algumas construções calcadas no latim e de trechos sobrecarregados; as imagens insólitas, por si mesmas, não prejudicam a oração." Six taken (17:33, 17:36b, 17:40, 17:41, 17:46, 17:48), two refused as options (17:34 aperfeiçoou, 17:35 ensina).

outcomes.remark: "fez imaculado o meu caminho" sounds calqued → "tornou imaculado o meu caminho"
outcomes.reason: Which verb Portuguese uses for pónere + adjective is grammar (D2); neither fazer nor tornar is the Latin's verb.

outcomes.remark: the vowels of "aperfeiçoou os" are hard to say every day → "Que tornou perfeitos os meus pés"
outcomes.reason: perfícere → aperfeiçoar is the glossary row, tried on this verse by the Ps 8 agent; "tornou perfeitos" would also say "tornou" twice in two verses after 17:33.

outcomes.remark: "ensinar as mãos para" leaves the ear expecting another construction → "Que instrui as minhas mãos para a batalha"
outcomes.reason: docére → ensinar (glossary), and the psalm echoes it: docet (17:35) … docébit (17:36b, "me ensinará"). instruir is erudíre's verb (2:10 row).

outcomes.remark: "ela mesma" between two pauses breaks the colon and sounds explanatory → "e a vossa própria disciplina me ensinará"
outcomes.reason: Order and form only; ipsa is kept.

outcomes.remark: the colon is heavy, "mim … mim" hammers, and "debaixo de mim" delays the object → "e derrubastes sob mim os que contra mim se levantavam"
outcomes.reason: Taken, and "sob" carried to all four places of subtus / sub so that the Latin's repetition stays one word.

outcomes.remark: WORST LINE: "dar alguém de costas" sounds like a body's position → "E me destes as costas dos meus inimigos"
outcomes.reason: All the Latin's words kept; a double accusative becomes a genitive (grammar).

outcomes.remark: "coxearam" is not current in Brazil and heavy → "envelheceram e mancaram"
outcomes.reason: With the blind reader, who did not know "coxearam". The comma before "e" is kept (the Latin's et joins a third verb after a pause).

outcomes.remark: the first colon piles up length and pauses → "Deus, que me dais vinganças e sujeitais os povos sob mim"
outcomes.reason: Article and comma dropped (vindíctas has none); "sob mim" for sub me.

audit.note: Stage two, draft 4, Portuguese only. 44 items, 10 unknown words (transporei, imaculado ×2, cingiu, cingistes, cervos, desfaleçam, coxearam, veredas, iníquo). Two real faults, both mended: 17:34 "cervos" heard as "servos" (→ corças), 17:44 "contradições" heard as inconsistencies (→ contendas). The rest are the Latin's own figures heard as the Latin reads: God "holy with the holy … perverse with the perverse" (17:26–27, which the Latin says), whose King and whose Christ (17:51), who magnifies (17:51), Christ and David as one or two (17:51, D19).

outcomes.remark: "Com o santo sereis santo" may sound like a change in God
outcomes.reason: The Latin's figure, word for word (eris); the reader himself heard "God deals holily with the holy" first.

outcomes.remark: "com o eleito sereis eleito" heard as God also being chosen
outcomes.reason: The Latin says exactly that (eléctus eris); Douay-Rheims "with the elect thou wilt be elect".

outcomes.remark: "com o perverso vos pervertereis" heard as God becoming perverse
outcomes.reason: The Latin's own jolt (pervertéris, Douay-Rheims "thou wilt be perverted"); the Latinist passed it; the explanation (Matos Soares's "como ele merece") is refused under D2 and kept as an option.

outcomes.remark: "os meus pés como os dos cervos" may be heard as "servos"
outcomes.reason: A homophone the listener cannot undo → "corças".

outcomes.remark: "a vossa disciplina": instruction, punishment, or God's self-control
outcomes.reason: disciplína (παιδεία) is both instruction and correction, and the verse says both (corrigiu … ensinará).

outcomes.remark: "as minhas pegadas" is usually the marks on the ground
outcomes.reason: The Latin's image (vestígia); the reader heard the sense, steps firm.

outcomes.remark: "me destes os meus inimigos de costas": fleeing or surrendered?
outcomes.reason: Mended with the stylist's wording, "as costas dos meus inimigos".

outcomes.remark: "as contradições do povo" heard as the people's inconsistencies, not opposition to the speaker
outcomes.reason: A wrong first hearing → "contendas".

outcomes.remark: "Os filhos estranhos": foreigners not perceived; heard as others' children or odd ones
outcomes.reason: aliénus is "not one's own" before it is "foreign" (glossary row aliénus → estranho, wider than estrangeiro); "others' children" is inside the Latin.

outcomes.remark: "exalte-se": that people exalt God, or God exalt himself
outcomes.reason: As 9:33 (the glossary's jussive); the reader heard the right one first.

outcomes.remark: "me dais vinganças": lets me avenge myself, or avenges me
outcomes.reason: The Latin (das vindíctas mihi) is open the same way.

outcomes.remark: who magnifies and shows mercy; whose King and whose Christ; "o seu Cristo, Davi" as Jesus, or as two persons
outcomes.reason: The Latin's participles hang on nothing and its possessives are as open; Christus → Cristo is settled (D19), and the Church has heard Christ in it.

outcomes.remark: unknown words: transporei; cingiu, cingistes (17:33, 17:40); desfaleçam (17:38); iníquo (17:49); veredas (17:46); imaculado (17:31, 17:33)
outcomes.reason: Each was paraphrased rightly in the same reply (transpor = get over an obstacle; desfaleçam = lose strength); cingir is the Latin's image of girding; iníquo, vereda, imaculado are glossary words.

outcomes.remark: unknown word: coxearam
outcomes.reason: → mancaram, with the stylist.

audit.note: Stage two, draft 5 (revise_v5.py; draft 4 kept as prayed.v4.json): 17:33 "e tornou imaculado o meu caminho"; 17:34 "como os das corças … e sobre as alturas me firmando" (new decision cervorum; the Latinist's gerund); 17:36b "e a vossa própria disciplina me ensinará" (new decision ipsa); subtus / sub → "sob" in 17:37, 39, 40, 48 (new decision subtus); 17:40 "e derrubastes sob mim os que contra mim se levantavam"; 17:41 "E me destes as costas dos meus inimigos"; 17:44 "das contendas do povo"; 17:46 "e mancaram"; 17:48 "Deus, que me dais vinganças e sujeitais os povos sob mim".

Draft 5, whole psalm, checks.py: exit 0 (hard pass). 17:40 second colon now +4 (sob mim, the stylist's order), 17:48 first colon within range. Rhyme flags only the two accepted in stage one (17:15, 17:13/14 — the Latin's own).

Stage two, the gate on draft 5 (part2/, 17:26–17:51). One verse, minor: 17:45 the tense of cognóvi — refused. Everything changed in draft 5 passes: corças, 'me firmando', 'tornou imaculado', 'a vossa própria disciplina', 'sob' ×4, 'as costas dos meus inimigos', 'contendas', 'mancaram', 'Deus, que me dais vinganças'. Gate passed, no major. Marks confirmed in all 27 verses.

outcomes.remark: 'que eu não conhecia' puts an imperfect for the Latin perfect cognóvi, adding a durative aspect (minor) → 'que eu não conheci'
outcomes.reason: cognóvi is the perfect of a verb of knowing whose perfect states knowledge (I have come to know = I know): the state is what 'não conhecia' says; 'que eu não conheci' is heard in Brazil as 'whom I never met'. Douay-Rheims 'which I knew not', Matos Soares 1932 'que eu não conhecia'.
